Check your book (the validator) What you're doing: giving your export a once-over with the same scepticism a store's ingestion machine will use — before it ever leaves your desk. Steps Open the Export dialog and pick the preset you'll actually ship. Choose Validate This Book . Read the results top-down: errors first, then warnings, then the passes. Every line is explained in plain language — what was checked, and if something failed, what to do about it. What it checks The mimetype entry is first in the package and stored uncompressed — the oldest EPUB rule there is. container.xml points at a package file that is actually there. Every XML and XHTML file is well-formed. The manifest and the files agree both ways: nothing declared is missing, nothing present is undeclared, no duplicate identifiers. The reading order (spine) resolves, end to end. The navigation document carries its landmarks — contents, body matter, and cover when a cover ships — and the legacy NCX is present with targets that resolve. Every internal link and anchor resolves, footnote back-links included. Every image carries alt text. Required metadata is present: title, author, identifier, language — and a declared cover is properly marked as the cover. Warnings are advice, not failure A missing cover, a missing description, or using the book's own identifier because there's no ISBN yet — the validator notes these as warnings, with the reason, and lets you ship anyway. Stores accept all three; the notes exist so the choices are yours, made knowingly. What can go wrong — and one honest limit The honest limit: this is structural validation. The full, official EPUBCheck suite runs on Beuk's servers in the SaaS phase — the validator will tell you so itself, in its own results panel. Beuk doesn't claim EPUBCheck's authority for a lighter set of checks. It passed here but a store complained. Stores add rules of their own on top of the standard (cover pixel sizes, file-size caps). Copy the store's exact words into the error decoder .
